text:
Alex W: Heads-up — after the kernel rewrite rolled at 06:40 UTC our prefix cache hit-rate tanked on the 13B family. Hit went from ~92% to ~61% and tail latency jumped. Suspecting a keying mismatch during warmboot.

Maria G: Ugh. Same deploy that switched the attention microkernel and changed the tensor pack order?

Alex W: Yep, that one. We see a lot of cache miss patterns that correspond to previously cached prefixes. Keys look similar but not identical.

Dan P: Can you paste one or two example keys (hex) before/after? Even truncated.

Alex W: From prod logs, old key: 3f7a9d0b::a1f4c2::len=128::model=v1.4
New key: 3f7a9d0b::a1f4c3::len=128::model=v1.4
Only a single nibble changed in the middle chunk for many entries.

Sophia L: That smells like a non-deterministic float packing / small rounding diff in the KV serializer or changed order in attention state serialization. The kernel rewrite changed the kv layout for fused-attn to be contiguous along head-major vs head-minor.

Maria G: bench-bot, do we have a before/after key histogram for the top 1000 prefixes?

bench-bot: Profiling report: prefix_key_entropy_histogram before deploy: top-1000 identical keys ratio=0.92; after deploy: identical keys ratio=0.61; most diffs concentrated in bytes 16..24.

Dan P: Bytes 16..24 map to the serialized KV slice for the last attention block. If packing axis changed, hash input changes.

Alex W: Confirmed by local repro: running a sample prompt with kernel_v2 toggled off yields the old key; kernel_v2 on yields the new key.

Maria G: Short-term mitigation: gate the kernel rewrite for Dedicated and Hosted until we fix key stability. Can we add a compatibility flag prefix_key_version that falls back to v1 matching?

Sophia L: We should also include model/kernel metadata in the cache key explicitly (e.g., "kern_ver=kvpack_v2"). That'll make mismatches explicit and avoid silent cache misses.

Dan P: Agreed. Long-term we need canonical serializer tests — roundtrip determinism across kernels and quant profiles. Also add a hash salt + version field so key collisions or silent changes surface in metrics.

Alex W: For immediate rollout: ops-bot can toggle the feature flag for us? Ops: can we flip host kernel_v2=false for hvm-prod-pool while we patch?

ops-bot: Flag change scheduled. Turning off kernel_v2 for pool hvm-prod @ 07:12 UTC.

Maria G: Patch plan: 1) Add explicit kern_ver tag to prefix key 2) Add unit test that serializes same KV state across kernels and quantization profiles and asserts identical bytes when kern_ver is same 3) Add migration script to warmbackfill cache for high-volume prompts or accept temporary misses.

Dan P: Also found a smaller-but-important issue: quantized kernels produce slightly trimmed trailing zeros in the serialized buffer (we used to pad to fixed length). That changed the input to the hash. We should normalize serialization to canonical fixed-length representation or include length fields deterministically.

Sophia L: For the warmup strategy: we can pre-warm popular prefixes after deploy by replaying top-10k prompts with kernel_v2 serialization to populate cache, but cost is non-trivial. Alternative: maintain a small compatibility cache mapping v1->v2 hashes for a while.

Alex W: Cost impact numbers from prod: 92%->61% hit drop increased token cost by ~2.8x for affected routes, and median p95 latency increased by 35ms. That's customer-visible. We need the gate ASAP.

Maria G: Who's owning the serializer change? Dan, Sophia — you two pair on a patch and add the unit/integration tests. Alex, coordinate rollout and monitor dashboards. Ops will hold the flag until green.

Dan P: Will do. Quick snippet I'm adding to ensure canonical hashing:
```python
def canonical_prefix_hash(kv_bytes, version):
    # pad to fixed 256B blocks, append explicit meta version
    padded = kv_bytes.ljust(256, b"\x00")
    meta = f"kern_ver={version}".encode()
    return hashlib.sha256(padded + meta).hexdigest()
```

Sophia L: Nice. I'll add tests for quantized vs fp16 vs int8 kernels to ensure they produce identical canonicalized bytes when expected.

Alex W: Thanks. After patch let's re-run bench suite and a limited canary on a small host pool. We should track realtime: prefix_cache_hit_rate, prefix_miss_ratio_by_kernver, and warm_miss_replay_cost.

Maria G: Also add alert: if hit-rate drops >10% vs baseline within 30m after deploy, auto-roll flag off.

Alex W: Agreed. I'll post updates here. Thanks all :thumbsup:

bench-bot: Canary run (post-flag-roll): hit-rate restored to 90.8% on canary pool at 07:40 UTC.

Alex W: Great — keeping flag off until we're sure tests & migration are in.

Maria G: Filing a short postmortem and a follow-up RFC for canonical KV serialization schema.

Alex W: Filing link: https://redwood.company/rfcs/kv-canonicalization (internal)

Sophia L: One last note — make sure we include model version and quant profile in key metadata; otherwise future quantization tweaks will cause same pain.

Alex W: Adding that to the RFC. End.
